title_en: 270: Sports, Markets and Investing: What Separates Skill From Good Luck
title_zh: 体育、市场与投资：是什么区分了技巧与好运——对话 BlackRock 固收组合经理 Ronald Van Loon
subtitle_zh: 从网球54%的每分胜率到足球、篮球，看微小优势如何复利成长期投资成功。
summary_zh: 本期 The Bid 由主持 Oscar Pulido 对话 BlackRock 全球固定收益团队（Global Fixed Income Group）组合经理 Ronald Van Loon，把今夏的体育盛景当作理解投资的镜子。核心论点是：成功投资不在于把每个决策都做对，而在于认清自己微小的优势（edge），并让它随时间复利累积。Van Loon 用网球举例：Roger Federer 生涯1,526场单打赢下近80%，但按分数算只赢了约54%；Sinner 与 Alcaraz 的每分成功率同样仅略高于54%，却拿下近三年12项大满贯中的10项。他们的研究显示，投资上只需53%的决策正确率就能跑出超额收益（outperformance），但必须把命中率（hit rate）与赔付结构（payout profile）放在一起看，并在破发点这类关键分上提高转化。足球说明单场比赛运气成分更高，可世界杯四强恰恰就是赛前最被看好的四支球队；夺冠的西班牙队8场进14球仅失1球、控球率约64%，印证团队打法胜过明星前锋——正如世界上150万只固定收益证券，需要信用分析师、风险经理与交易员协作传球。篮球则展示了20年来三分出手占比从17%升至40%，即按期望值（概率乘以赔付）重新配置出手。这一集把成功概率、赔付结构与决策次数三个维度串成一套可复用的投资框架。

turns.en: And the reason for that really is in tennis, you have lots of opportunities to score. You have a tournament, several matches, matches made up of sets, setters made up of games, games made up of points. Each of these is an opportunity to express a difference in skill.

turns.en: And then once you start adding these kind of measurement points together, it starts compounding up and you end up with a very high probability of winning the match like in Federer's case, 80%. Now, in investing, we have a similar dynamic on a portfolio manager.

And then the third element of course is the pass rate and the way that Spain played had a comfortably much higher than average pass rate and also much higher than average success

turns.en: for pass rate. So that's a very unique style of playing and very different to the other four semi-finals. And obviously it proved successful. I think you can translate that over to the world of investing as well. I'm a bond manager, I'm working in fixed income.
turns.zh: 水平。所以这是一种非常独特的踢法，跟其他几支四强球队非常不同，而且显然，它被证明是成功的。我觉得这一点也可以搬到投资世界里。我是一名债券基金经理，我在固定收益（fixed income）领域工作。

turns.en: In the words of our CIO rig reader, he says there's something like one and a half million fixed income securities in the world. That's an enormous breadth and width of investment options you have on the table there. It's pretty obvious you are not very likely to win that game with a star striker approach or with a long ball.
turns.zh: 用我们的首席投资官（CIO）Rick Rieder 的话说，世界上大概有150万只固定收益证券。摆在你桌上的投资选项，其广度和宽度是巨大的。很显然，你不太可能靠明星前锋（star striker）的打法、或者靠长传冲吊（long ball）去赢下这场比赛。

turns.en: You're really going to have to win that game through the team because simply the width and the breadth of the investment opportunities are too broad. So indeed we have specialists, each of their own function, we have credit analysts looking at the credits, we have risk managers looking at position sizing, we have traders looking
turns.zh: 你真的必须靠团队去赢下这场比赛，因为投资机会的广度和宽度实在太大了。所以我们确实有一批各有分工的专家：有信用分析师（credit analyst）看信用债，有风险经理（risk manager）看仓位大小，有交易员看

turns.en: at execution and then we can pass the security so to say in between these specialists. So I think that's clearly an analogy there. My own way to think about it is that there's one and a half million fixed income securities in the world that offers you one and a half million opportunities to score. Right.
turns.zh: 执行。然后我们就可以在这些专家之间，可以说是把证券『传』来『传』去。所以我觉得这里显然有一个类比。我自己的理解方式是：世界上有150万只固定收益证券，也就给了你150万次得分机会。对。

turns.en: And going back to the beginning of our conversation, you don't necessarily have to make every single decision, the right decision. In other words, in a portfolio, you may not own one and a half million securities. That's unlikely you're going to own far less than that.
turns.zh: 回到我们对话的开头：你不一定非要把每一个决策都做对。换句话说，在一个组合里，你未必会持有150万只证券——那不太可能，你持有的数量会远远少于这个。

turns.en: But there still gives you a lot of chances where you could get either the right decision or the wrong decision. But so long as you're getting a little bit more than half of the decisions right, you're probably trending in the right direction. So let's keep talking about sports. The Olympics are coming up in 2028.
turns.zh: 但它仍然给了你很多机会，让你可能做对、也可能做错。不过只要你做对的决策比一半稍多一点，你大概率就是朝着正确的方向在走。那我们继续聊体育。2028年奥运会（Olympics）就要来了。

turns.en: And the Olympics are interesting because for many athletes, there's years of preparation that come down to a single race, a single match or a single performance. And that's again, very different from tennis where you have hundreds of opportunities to score.
turns.zh: 奥运会很有意思，因为对很多运动员来说，多年的准备最后都归结为一场比赛、一次对决或者一次表现。这又和网球非常不同——网球里你有几百次得分机会。

turns.en: So what can that teach us about preparation and decision making when you may only have one opportunity to get it right? Yes, of course, it's super different to the world of investing, right? And investing your measure continuously almost in the Olympics, as you say, you have
turns.zh: 那么，当你可能只有一次机会把它做对时，这能在准备和决策方面教给我们什么？是的，当然，这跟投资世界非常不一样。投资里你几乎是被持续不断地衡量的；而在奥运会上，就像你说的，你只有

turns.en: that one moment, one moment in time that you prepare for for a long time. But I think it's quite interesting how the world of sports itself has adjusted to deal with that challenge. If you look at some of the Olympic sports, particularly perhaps the one that are a bit
turns.zh: 那一个时刻，一个你为之准备了很长时间的时间点。但我觉得很有意思的是，体育界自己已经做了调整来应对这个挑战。如果你看一些奥运项目，特别是那些相对

turns.en: less popular that don't have like annual international tournaments, the way how those sports are set up is that, particularly in the year prior to the Olympics, you see a sudden increase in the amount of international tournaments, think about qualification tournaments or ranking tournaments.
turns.zh: 冷门、没有每年一度的国际赛事的项目，这些运动的安排方式是：特别是在奥运会前一年，你会看到国际赛事数量突然增加，比如资格赛（qualification tournament）或者排名赛（ranking tournament）。

turns.en: So what these tournaments offer to the participant is really two things. So one, the opportunity to learn about yourself and where your skill is and two, the opportunity to learn about the skill of your opponent. And that really makes the Olympics itself like an outcome of a process, the actual
turns.zh: 这些赛事真正给参赛者的是两样东西：第一，一个了解自己、了解自己水平在哪里的机会；第二，一个了解对手水平的机会。这就使得奥运会本身更像是一个过程的结果，实际的

turns.en: match or whatever they participate in is the outcome. And it's then that pre-Elympic circuit, really, that is the process through which you learn about your relative skill. And there's a similarity then or a parallel to an investment process that an investment team would use.
turns.zh: 那场比赛或者他们参加的任何赛事，是结果；而奥运之前的这一系列巡回赛，才是那个过程——你在这个过程中了解自己的相对水平。这里就有一个相似点，或者说平行之处，跟投资团队所使用的投资流程（investment process）很像。

turns.en: And you mentioned you're a bond manager, a fixed income manager. There is a process behind the scenes that you're following to try and increase your chances of success. Yes, absolutely. Continuous learning and continuous adapting to the environment because not only your own
turns.zh: 你提到你是一名债券基金经理、固定收益基金经理。在幕后，你遵循着一套流程，来尽量提高自己成功的概率。是的，完全正确。持续学习、持续适应环境，因为不只是你自己的

turns.en: relative skill changes, it's also your opponent's changes all the time. So that's that continuously learning process means that you have to all the time adjust. So again, we've continued to broaden the conversation. When we originally spoke, Ronald, it was about tennis and we started there. We've talked about soccer.
turns.zh: 相对水平在变化，对手的水平也一直在变。所以这种持续学习的过程意味着你必须不停地调整。所以说，我们的话题一直在拓宽。最初我们对谈的时候，Ronald，聊的是网球，我们从那里开始；后来我们聊了足球，

turns.en: We've talked about the World Cup and team-based approaches. We've talked about the Olympics, which introduces this concept of a process that you need to follow to therefore be ready for that singular match or game or event that you've been building towards.
turns.zh: 聊了世界杯和以团队为基础的打法；也聊了奥运会——它引入了『流程』这个概念：你需要遵循一套流程，才能为那个你一直在为之准备的单场比赛、单场对决或单个赛事做好准备。

turns.en: But let's talk about basketball, which has given us plenty to talk about is for those of us based here in New York, like myself, the New York Knicks won the NBA championship this summer. And I can certainly tell you, Ronald, that New York was a buzz when that took place.
turns.zh: 不过我们来聊聊篮球吧。对我们这些常驻纽约的人来说——比如我——篮球给了太多谈资：New York Knicks 今年夏天拿下了 NBA 总冠军。我可以肯定地告诉你，Ronald，那一刻整个纽约都沸腾了。

turns.en: Basketball is unique in that it gives us another way of thinking about decision-making because not every shot offers the same potential reward. There are ways in which to score two points in basketball or in some cases, three points. So how should investors think about the trade-off between the probability of being right
turns.zh: 篮球的独特之处在于，它给了我们另一种思考决策的方式，因为不是每一次投篮都提供同样的潜在回报。在篮球里，你可以得2分，某些情况下可以得3分。那么，投资者该如何思考『做对的概率』和

turns.en: and the potential payoff when they are? Yeah, that's a super interesting basketball. And there's also a great analogy. So if you think about the game of basketball today and then compare it to maybe how the NBA was 20 years ago, there has definitely been a big change.
turns.zh: 『做对时的潜在赔付』之间的取舍（trade-off）？是的，篮球非常有意思，也是一个很好的类比。如果你想想今天的篮球比赛，再和20年前的 NBA 做个比较，变化确实非常大。

turns.en: For example, two decades ago, the number of three-point attempts that were made just beyond the circle in basketball was about 17% of total shots. And if you translate that to the NBA game today, that's more than double, that is 40%. So that means is that the percentage of shot attempts that are being made just beyond
turns.zh: 举例来说，20年前，在三分线弧顶外出手的三分球，大约占总出手数的17%。而换算到今天的 NBA 比赛，这个数字翻了一倍还多，达到了40%。这意味着，在

turns.en: the three-point line is more than doubled. The number of shot attempts that are made just below the basket is just about the same. And it's really that mid-range, really, where you see a decrease. So like the two-point jumper, so to say, that's exactly the reason why that is a trade-off
turns.zh: 三分线外的出手占比翻了一倍多；而在篮下附近的出手数量基本没变。真正下降的是中距离（mid-range），也就是所谓的中距离两分跳投（two-point jumper）。这恰恰就是那个取舍的原因——

turns.en: between the probability of making the shots and the payoff of when you do make the shots. Obviously, it is a bit more difficult to take a three-point shot and be successful in that. Then it is a two-point shot, but as you rightly say, your payoff is 50% higher.
turns.zh: 投篮命中的概率和投进之后的赔付之间的取舍。显然，投三分并且投进，要比投两分更难一些，但就像你说的，你的赔付要高出50%。

turns.en: So once you actually start translating that into expected value, so to say, right, probability times payoff, then indeed, the game has shown that it's the three-point shots and the right underneath the basket shots, the expected value is the highest. And the game is migrated very much the same as the analogy as we just had in tennis
turns.zh: 所以一旦你真的把它换算成期望值（expected value），也就是概率乘以赔付，那么比赛确实已经证明：三分球和篮下正下方的投篮，期望值最高。整个比赛的打法已经迁移了，这和我们刚才在网球里

turns.en: or we just had in football. You need to look at the probability of scoring and look at the payoff, marry those together. And then last point, of course, is look at how many shots attempts you can possibly make. And you can really see the game of basketball really migrated on those three same dimensions
turns.zh: 或者在足球里讲到的类比非常相似。你需要看得分概率，也看赔付，把两者结合起来；最后一点当然是看你尽可能能出手多少次。你确实能看到，篮球这项运动就是沿着这三个相同的维度发生了迁移，

turns.en: to a different game today than it was two decades ago. Ronald, when you put all of this together, again, from the small edges that you get from a sport like tennis, which provides hundreds of opportunities in a match to the teamwork element of soccer, the different potential payoffs from a sport like basketball.
turns.zh: 今天的篮球已经和20年前不是一项同样的比赛了。Ronald，当你把这一切放在一起看——从网球这种一场比赛提供几百次机会的运动里得到的微小优势，到足球里的团队协作要素，再到篮球这种运动里不同的潜在赔付——

turns.en: What is it that elites sport ultimately teaches us about becoming a better investor? If you look at the three sports, really, look at them together, I think there's some big lessons to take away as an investor. You can almost break it up in three bits. You look at the probability of success per investment decision.
turns.zh: 精英体育最终在『成为更好的投资者』这件事上，究竟教给了我们什么？如果你把这三项运动放在一起看，我觉得作为投资者能带走一些很重要的经验。你几乎可以把它拆成三块：第一，看每个投资决策的成功概率；

turns.en: You look at the payoff profile of the investment decisions. What's the payoff? If you're successful, what's the payoff? If you are unsuccessful. And then lastly is the number of goal attempts on the number of the investment decisions that the game provides you. And I think the key message really here is bit like in basketball.
turns.zh: 第二，看投资决策的赔付结构（payoff profile）：如果你成功了，赔付是多少？如果你失败了，赔付又是多少？最后是这场『比赛』给你提供的射门次数，也就是投资决策的数量。我觉得这里真正的关键信息，有点像篮球里那样：

turns.en: You need to look at these together. There's no point in focusing on just one aspect of an equation. You need to look at all three together and choose your optimum that works for you across all these three dimensions together. And I think the second point, which is really valid, is that the investment skill,
turns.zh: 你必须把它们放在一起看。只盯着这个等式里的某一方面是没有意义的。你要把三者放在一起看，并在这三个维度上一起选出对你最合适的最优解。我觉得第二点也非常成立：你在每个投资决策上需要具备的投资技巧，

turns.en: that you need to have per investment decision needs to be only marginally above a coin toss. As long as, of course, you let them compound over time. It's a bit like in tennis as you let these investment decisions compound over time. You already need to be successful 53, 54% of the time.
turns.zh: 只需要比抛硬币稍微高一点点就够了——当然，前提是你要让它们随时间复利累积。这有点像网球：当你让这些投资决策随时间复利累积时，你只需要有53%、54%的时间是成功的，

turns.en: And that leads you to this kind of durable high wind rates over the long term. Well, all the sports that we've talked about are definitely contact sports. Ronald, you and I have worked in the markets for many years. And I think we can attest to the fact that investing is also a full contact sport.
turns.zh: 长期下来就能带来那种持久的、很高的胜率（win rate）。我们聊的这些运动，毫无疑问都是身体接触类运动（contact sport）。Ronald，你和我都在市场里干了很多年，我觉得我们可以作证：投资同样是一项全方位身体对抗的运动。

turns.en: That's volatility that will introduce itself once in a while that can make it a very emotional exercise, but having discipline and thinking about some of the process and relying on your team. Some of the things that you've talked about will help. Ronald, I'm just curious when you go and attend a sporting match,
turns.zh: 波动率（volatility）时不时就会冒出来，让这件事变得非常情绪化；但保持纪律、想着那些流程、依靠你的团队——你刚才讲到的这些东西会有帮助。Ronald，我只是好奇，当你去现场看一场体育比赛的时候，

turns.en: can you just enjoy the game or is your mind racing about the analogy to investing? Yes. You have to ask the people that join me and I've heard that comment once or twice. So I think you'll probably onto something there. I'm sure your mind is spinning. But we're thankful that it is because you've given us a lot of great analogies
turns.zh: 你能纯粹享受比赛吗，还是脑子里在飞速联想投资的类比？是的。你得去问跟我一起看球的人——这样的话我听过一两次，所以我觉得你大概说中了什么。我相信你的脑子确实在转，但我们也很感谢它在转，因为你给了我们很多很棒的类比，

turns.en: and a lot of great comparisons between sport and investing. Thank you for rejoining us on the bid to talk about this topic. And we look forward to having you back when you have another great story to tell us about these two themes together. Ronald, thank you again for joining us. Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 以及很多把体育和投资做的精彩比较。谢谢你再次来到 The Bid 聊这个话题。我们期待你下次再带着另一个把这两个主题结合在一起的好故事回来。Ronald，再次感谢你的参与。非常感谢。
